subject: City Council Charter Provisions
overview: The Medford Charter Study Committee met to review comparative data on city council charter provisions and plan upcoming community engagement efforts. The committee voted to submit an official response statement regarding proposed City Council charter amendments and heard an announcement of co-chair Laurel Siegel's resignation.

items.title: Approval of April Meeting Minutes
items.summary: The committee approved the minutes from its April meeting.

items.title: Presentation on City Council Charter Provisions
items.summary: Representatives from the Collins Center presented a comparative analysis of city council powers, compensation, staffing, and reorganization authority across several Massachusetts municipality charters.

items.title: Response to Proposed City Council Charter Amendments
items.summary: The committee voted to adopt a formal statement declining to take a stance on the City Council's proposed charter amendments prior to public input, submitting the response for the City Council record.

items.title: Public Information Session and Community Outreach Planning
items.summary: Members discussed logistics for the June 8 public information session, flyer distribution, social media outreach, and plans to interview current and former city officials.

items.title: Resignation Announcement
items.summary: Co-chair Laurel Siegel announced her resignation from the committee due to taking a new position as Community Development Block Grant manager for the City of Medford.
